# Falsy

<link-summary>The values JavaScript treats as false in a boolean context.</link-summary>

<web-summary>Falsy — The values JavaScript treats as false in a boolean context. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/array</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
type Falsy = false | null | undefined | 0 | 0n | "";
```

`false`, `null`, `undefined`, `0`, `0n` and the empty string. The type exists so that `compact` can say what it removes and return a narrowed array without a cast; `NaN` is falsy too but has no place in a type, since its type is `number`.

## Examples

### Shape

```javascript
const values = [0, "", false, null, undefined];
```
